artworks.title: Automedon with the Horses of Achilles
artworks.description: Regnault's Boston masterpiece: Automedon masters Xanthus and Balius — Achilles' immortal horses — before the chariot that will carry Patroclus to death and Achilles to Hector. The charioteer Homer honoured most after Patroclus made flesh in Second Empire paint.

artworks.title: Automedon with the Horses of Achilles (alternate view)
artworks.description: Another photograph of the same MFA canvas: muscle, rein and horseflesh — Automedon as the human hinge between Achilles' wrath and the battlefield.

artworks.title: Sketch for Automedon with the Horses of Achilles
artworks.description: Regnault's oil sketch for the finished Automedon — the charioteer already wrestling the immortal team into a single composition.

artworks.title: Esquisse pour Automédon avec les chevaux d'Achille
artworks.description: French study for the same subject: Automédon named in the title — the Iliadic driver as a nineteenth-century academic trial before the Boston canvas.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer makes Automedon son of Diores the charioteer of Achilles' horses — the man who yokes Xanthus and Balius and fights on after Patroclus falls.

popCulture.title: Automedon
popCulture.description: Achilles' charioteer — not the butterfly or fire-engine namesakes that share his name in modern catalogs.
